proved_step:
statement: For every integer N>=1, every language F subset {0,1}^N, every prefix u of length t<N, and each b in {0,1}, if R_u={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: uz in F}, then R_{ub}={z in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bz in R_u}.
proof: Fix any suffix z of length N-t-1. By definition, z belongs to R_{ub} iff ubz belongs to F. Also by definition, bz belongs to R_u iff ubz belongs to F. Thus z belongs to R_{ub} iff z belongs to {z': bz' in R_u}. This holds for every suffix z, so the sets are equal.
evidence: Direct general proof; finite independent verification at N=4 checked 65,536 languages and 1,966,080 reachable transitions (cm-b0ec472e8e0648d7).

statement: For every N>=1, every language F subset {0,1}^N, and every 0<=t<N, if D_t is the number of distinct residual languages R_u={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: uz in F} over prefixes u of length t, then D_{t+1}<=2D_t. Proof: each residual R at cut t has at most two derivatives R_b={z: bz in R}, one for each b in {0,1}; every residual at cut t+1 equals one of these derivatives, so the set of distinct residuals at t+1 has size at most twice the number at t.
proof: Each distinct residual R at cut t has at most two one-bit derivatives R_b={z:bz in R}, for b in {0,1}. By the residual transition identity, every residual at cut t+1 is one of those derivatives. Taking the union over the D_t residuals gives at most 2D_t distinct residuals.
scope: All finite Boolean languages of fixed length N; no computational hypothesis.
evidence: Complete direct proof; finite discovery check requested separately.

statement: For integers N>=1 and 0<=t<=N, the maximum over languages F subset {0,1}^N of D_t(F), the number of distinct residual rows indexed by prefixes u of length t, is min(2^t, 2^(2^(N-t))).
proof: There are 2^t prefixes and exactly 2^(2^(N-t)) Boolean functions on the suffix set {0,1}^{N-t}, so D_t(F) is at most their minimum. Let r be that minimum. Choose r distinct Boolean rows on the suffix set and assign them to r distinct prefixes; assign any one chosen row to each remaining prefix. Define F to contain exactly those concatenated prefix-suffix pairs whose row entry is 1. The residual rows of this F are exactly the assigned rows, so D_t(F)=r. This also covers t=0 and t=N.
scope: All fixed-length Boolean languages, every cut 0<=t<=N; no computational hypothesis.
evidence: General construction and counting proof. Discovery check at N=4 reported widths [1,2,4,4,2] (cm-5b7abd5dbef54896); finite check is corroboration only.

evidence: The proof is a direct extensional equality: for any suffix z of length N-t-1, z ∈ R_{ub} ⇔ ubz ∈ F ⇔ bz ∈ R_u ⇔ z ∈ {z' : bz' ∈ R_u}. This holds for all z, so the sets are equal. The finite verification at N=4 (cm-b0ec472e8e0648d7) checked 65,536 languages and 1,966,080 transitions with no violation. No argument gap exists; the statement is a basic definitional identity in the algebra of residual languages.

Each distinct residual R at cut t has at most two one-bit derivatives R_b={z:bz in R} for b in {0,1}. By S0001 (residual transition identity), every residual at cut t+1 is exactly one of these derivatives. Taking the union over the D_t distinct residuals at cut t gives at most 2D_t distinct residuals at cut t+1. This is a direct consequence of the definition and S0001. No counterexample exists; the finite check requested separately would only corroborate this logical consequence.

Upper bound: there are only 2^t prefixes and 2^(2^(N-t)) Boolean functions on suffixes, so D_t(F) ≤ min(2^t, 2^(2^(N-t))). Lower bound (achievability): let r = min(2^t, 2^(N-t)). Choose r distinct Boolean functions on {0,1}^{N-t} and assign them to r distinct prefixes of length t; assign an arbitrary chosen function to remaining prefixes. Define F as the set of prefix-suffix pairs where the assigned function evaluates to 1. Then F has exactly r distinct residual rows at cut t. The construction works for all t including t=0 and t=N. The finite check at N=4 (cm-5b7abd5dbef54896) reported widths [1,2,4,4,2] matching the formula. This is a complete combinatorial characterization.

proved_step:
statement: For every N>=1, language F subseteq {0,1}^N, cut t in {0,...,N}, and deterministic one-pass streaming decider whose state after reading a prefix depends only on that prefix, the number of distinct states reached after length-t prefixes is at least D_t(F), the number of distinct residual languages R_u={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: uz in F}. A layered residual-state machine attains D_t(F) states at cut t.
proof: If length-t prefixes u and v have distinct residuals, some suffix z belongs to exactly one of R_u,R_v. Exactly one of uz,vz is in F. If the machine reached the same state after u and v, determinism would give the same acceptance result on continuation z, a contradiction. So distinct residuals require distinct states. For attainability, store R_u after reading u; on bit b update R to R_b={z: bz in R}. At length N accept iff the empty suffix belongs to the current residual. The residual definition ensures correctness, and there is exactly one state per distinct residual at each layer.
scope: Finite Boolean languages of fixed length; deterministic exact one-pass machines, with state interpreted at a fixed cut. This gives no time or circuit-size lower bound without an additional encoding/update-cost theorem.

statement: For every finite Boolean language F subseteq {0,1}^N with k=|F| and every cut t in {0,...,N}, the number D_t(F) of distinct residuals R_u={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: uz in F} over length-t prefixes satisfies D_t(F) <= k+1. Proof: A nonempty residual R_u contains some suffix z, and then uz is an element of F whose length-t prefix is u. Thus every prefix u with nonempty residual is a length-t prefix of at least one word of F. There are at most k such prefixes, hence at most k distinct nonempty residuals. There is at most one additional residual, the empty set, so D_t(F)<=k+1. This includes F=empty and cuts t=0,N. Scope: fixed-length finite Boolean languages; state-count bound only, with no circuit/update-time implication.

statement: For every N>=1, F subseteq {0,1}^N, and cut 0<=t<=N, let D_t(F) be the number of distinct residuals R_u={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: uz in F}. Then D_t(F)<=min(2^t, 2^{N-t}, |F|+1). Proof: There are 2^t length-t prefixes, so at most 2^t residuals. Every residual is a subset of the 2^{N-t} suffixes, but this alone gives 2^{2^{N-t}} possible sets; instead, each nonempty residual contains a suffix and therefore corresponds to at least one word uz in F. Distinct nonempty residuals must arise from distinct prefixes, and each such prefix contains at least one distinct word of F, so there are at most min(2^t,|F|) nonempty residuals. There is at most one empty residual. Thus D_t(F)<=min(2^t,|F|)+1. Also, each residual is a subset of F's suffix set, whose size is at most |F|, so this does not establish the stated 2^{N-t} term; the valid conclusion is D_t(F)<=min(2^t,|F|)+1. Scope: fixed-length finite Boolean languages; this is a state-count upper bound and implies no update-time or circuit-size bound.

lemma: Residual count bound with proof: Let N>=1, F subseteq {0,1}^N, and 0<=t<=N. For each length-t prefix u let R_u={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: uz in F}, and let D_t(F) count distinct residuals. Then D_t(F)<=min(2^t,|F|)+1. Proof: There are at most 2^t residuals because there are that many prefixes. For each distinct nonempty residual choose one inducing prefix u and one suffix z in it. The word uz belongs to F. Distinct residuals have distinct chosen prefixes, because a prefix determines a unique residual; therefore the chosen words are distinct and the number of nonempty residuals is at most |F|. There is at most one empty residual. The bound follows. Scope is fixed-length finite Boolean languages; no update-cost implication.
